thread.title_full: Ohio House passes bill to update excavation safety laws

author: K. T. Blue
title: Ohio House passes bill to update excavation safety laws
text:
State Rep. Monica Robb Blasdel | The Ohio House of Representatives
State Rep. Monica Robb Blasdel | The Ohio House of Representatives
The Ohio House of Representatives has approved House Bill 227, which aims to improve excavation safety standards and restore the state’s eligibility for federal pipeline safety grant funding. The bill was announced by State Representatives Monica Robb Blasdel (R-New Waterford) and Mark Johnson (R-Chillicothe).
House Bill 227 proposes updates to the Ohio Revised Code regarding regulated excavation activities. The changes are intended to enhance public safety, improve coordination between excavators and utility operators, and ensure Ohio complies with federal standards set by the U.S. Department of Transportation.
“This legislation is about safety, flexibility, and modernization,” said Rep. Robb Blasdel. “By updating Ohio’s excavation laws, we’re giving operators the time and clarity they need to work safely and helping Ohio regain access to federal funding that promotes damage prevention.”
Under the bill, utility operators will have two full working days, not including the day of notification, to respond to excavation notices and mark underground utilities. The timeframe for beginning excavation will be extended from 10 working days to 16 calendar days, providing more flexibility for project planning. Additionally, the bill updates the definition of “excavation” by removing outdated blanket exemptions and specifying shallow-depth activities under twelve inches. References to “Limited Basis Participants,” a term no longer used in the industry, are also removed.
“By aligning Ohio law with federal standards, we’re ensuring safer worksites and unlocking new opportunities for federal support,” said Rep. Johnson.
The legislation will now proceed to the Ohio Senate for further consideration.
